member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.ChannelRegistry
member.summary: Plugin messaging channels (Paper's Messenger, sendPluginMessage). listens on a channel: the messages that the clients send on it arrive in the handler. The engine tells the clients which channels are listened on (minecraft:register). Send with .
member.remarks: Refused: the minecraft:* channels (a client's own registrations are read through ), velocity:* and bungeecord:*. Messages arrive in the tick window, in order per player, within the budgets of scripting.channels (a message beyond them is dropped). A listener ends with its plugin (unload or reload). Tick thread only. The worker delivers the messages; the in-process runtime does not.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.ChatRoute
member.summary: Restricts who gets a chat message while its handler runs. Signed chat stays signed: a restricted line is sent to the listed players only, as the engine's own private messages are.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.ChatRoute.Restrict(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Mc.Scripting.Player})
member.summary: Restricts the recipients of the chat message of the running handler. Only the listed players get the line. Works in a or a handler; the restriction applies to that one message only and ends when the dispatch is over. A second call replaces the list. An empty list means nobody gets the line. Offline handles are left out.
member.param: The players who get the message (at most 4096).
member.returns: The number of distinct recipients kept; -1 when no PlayerChat or PrivateMessage handler is running, or when the engine refuses the list.
member.exception: More than 4096 recipients. Nothing is sent to the engine.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.ChatRoute.Audience
member.summary: The audience of the running handler: the players who would get the line now. Without a restriction that is every player who accepts chat (a line); after it is the restricted list. Offline profiles are left out.
member.returns: The audience, sorted by profile id. Empty when no PlayerChat handler is running, and for a PrivateMessage handler that has not restricted its copy yet (that copy goes to the two players only).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Chat
member.summary: Chat lines that no player signed: the disguised chat the console's /say sends. The chat type picks the vanilla format and the name and message are shown in it. Use it for lines that are not a player's own words (a notice in a staff channel, a relayed message). The line is unsigned and has no signature marker, so it is never shown as a player's verified chat; for a player's own words use the chat event instead.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Chat.SendTo(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Mc.Scripting.Player},Mc.Scripting.ChatKind,Mc.Scripting.Text.Component,Mc.Scripting.Text.Component,Mc.Scripting.Text.Component)
member.summary: Sends an unsigned chat line to some players. The line is formatted from and (the sender's name as the line shows it) and . The message kinds (, , , ) need (the other side's name, as the vanilla format shows it); without one the call returns -1. Players who do not accept chat are skipped.
member.param: The players who get the line (at most 4096). Offline handles are left out.
The chat type of the line.
The sender name shown in the line.
The second name for a message kind; null for the others.
member.returns: The number of players the line reached; -1 when the engine refuses the call (a missing target for a message kind, an unknown kind).
member.exception: More than 4096 recipients. Nothing is sent to the engine.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.ChatMute
member.summary: Chat mutes. The engine keeps the mute table itself (it survives plugin reloads and server restarts) and refuses a muted player's chat lines, /say, /me and private messages before a plugin sees them, so a plugin does not check mutes on the message path. Commands and other actions are not affected. The reason is what the engine's mute notice (chat.mute_notice) can show the player. Thread: tick thread.

member.param: When the mute ends; null = forever.

member.exception: The expiry is not in the future, or the reason is longer than 256 UTF-8 bytes. Nothing is changed.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Content.CustomBlock
member.summary: A custom block: a state of a vanilla block that vanilla play seldom produces (and never turns a block into: the engine guards it), with its own hardness, drops and behaviour. The world stores a plain vanilla block state (so a server without the plugin shows a note block, never a corrupt chunk); a resource pack gives that state its own model ().

remarks.para: Which state. Custom blocks live in the note block's states with a mob head instrument (the ones nobody gets without a head above the block), 175 of them, handed out in registration order and remembered in the file named by content.state_file in Ramjet.toml, so the same id gets the same state after a restart. names the family: only minecraft:note_block exists in this version. While a block is registered the vanilla note block behaviour (tuning, notes, the instrument following the block below) is suppressed for its state.

Mining. The server decides how long a block takes to break, from ; the client predicts it from the note block (hardness 0.8), so a block that takes much longer than that appears to break on the client and comes back (the server refuses to finish it early): keep custom hardness near 0.8 or lower for smooth mining.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Content.ResourcePackBuilder
member.summary: Builds the resource pack zip that goes with custom content: item definitions, models, textures, language files and the block state remap of custom blocks. The output is deterministic (sorted entries, fixed timestamps), so the same input gives the same SHA-1 and clients keep their cached copy until something changes.

example.code: var pack = ResourcePackBuilder.Create("myplugin") .Description("My plugin") .AddItem(ruby, PackImage.Solid(0xFFE0115F)) .AddCustomBlock(rubyOre, PackImage.Checker(0xFF8B0A3C, 0xFFE0115F)) .AddLang("en_us", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["item.myplugin.ruby"] = "Ruby" }) .Build(); pack.SendTo(player); // hosted by ResourcePackHost (content.pack_host_port), or pack.ToResourcePack(yourUrl)

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Content.ResourcePackHost

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.McPluginAttribute
member.summary: The manifest of a source plugin (a .cs file or folder the server compiles at startup), written as an assembly attribute at the top of one of its files: [assembly: McPlugin("homes", version: "1.2.0", depends: ["economy >=1.0"])]. It carries the same information as plugin.json (a plugin.json next to the sources takes precedence). The server reads it from the syntax of the file before compiling, to compute the load order, so every argument must be a literal: string literals, null, and arrays or collection expressions of string literals (no constants, no nameof, no interpolation).
member.remarks: The attribute is ignored on a compiled plugin (it has a plugin.json or ).

member.summary: Registers (or re-binds) a plain-data component backed by a flecs component. Keys are global ("myplugin:health"); registering the same key with the same layout (field types and offsets) after a hot reload keeps existing component values. A changed layout drops the values, but is refused while another plugin is also bound to the key. Engine components can be bound by their registered name as long as the layout matches.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Edit
member.summary: Bulk region edits run by the engine in slices of the tick budget (for WorldEdit-style plugins). A plugin builds the request (the WEJB binary format of the engine's edit module) and submits it; the engine validates every field, applies the job, and records what it changed so the owner can undo it. Nothing here touches blocks one at a time: a request is one call, whatever its size. Tick thread only. The owner is always a player: the engine keeps history and clipboards per player.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.IEvent
member.summary: An event type. Catalogue events are ref structs: a handler gets the event by reference and can neither store it nor capture it in a closure or an async method, so the borrowed native data it carries (strings, byte buffers) cannot outlive the dispatch. Plugin-defined events are ordinary blittable structs that start with an field (or ref structs of the same layout).
member.remarks: Catalogue events are the engine's built-in events (fixed ids). Plugins can declare their own events: implement (e.g. "myplugin:thing") and leave at 0; an id is assigned at runtime.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerPreLoginEvent
member.summary: A client finished authentication and is about to enter the configuration phase. Handlers run on the TICK thread: a blocking call (a database or web lookup) freezes the whole server, so do not look anything up here. Cancel to refuse the login (set the kick message first), or call Defer() and answer later from Scheduler.RunAsync: the login waits up to 30 seconds, continues when every deferral allowed it and is refused as soon as one denies. A plugin that unloads releases its pending deferrals (counted as allowed).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerPreLoginEvent.Defer
member.summary: Holds the login until the returned is completed (up to the server's login timeout, 30 seconds). Use it to decide asynchronously (database or web lookups): call and complete the deferral from any thread. Cancelling the event instead refuses the login at once.
member.returns: The deferral to complete with or .

SenderName, ChatType, Decoration and the filter fields restyle the signed line without unsigning it: the signature covers only the typed text. The recipients are read with chat_recipients (ChatRoute.Audience) and narrowed with chat_restrict_recipients (ChatRoute.Restrict).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerKickEvent
member.summary: A player is about to be kicked: by a command or a plugin (cause Command or Plugin), or by the server itself for idling (Idle), floating (Flying), an invalid movement (InvalidMovement) or another server decision (Other). Cancel keeps the player for Command, Plugin, Idle and Flying; it is ignored for InvalidMovement and Other, whose disconnect is a protocol decision. The reason and the leave message may be changed for every cause. Not fired for protocol errors, login refusals or the disconnect at shutdown.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.EntityDeathEvent
member.summary: A living entity is dying (its health is 0). Fired before the death message, the kill credit and the drops, and before the death sounds. Cancel keeps it alive at 1 health: no death, no kill credit, no drops and no death sound. Plugins see CombatTagEnd (cause Death) after this event, not before it: a cancelled death does not end the combat tag. drop_experience and drop_items decide a mob's drops; a player's drops are decided by PlayerDeath, so these two fields are ignored for players.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.WeatherChangeEvent
member.summary: The rain of a world became visible or stopped being visible: it fires when the rain level crosses 0.2, about 20 ticks after the rain starts and up to about 80 ticks after it stops (the level moves 0.01 a tick). Keep the names to show: a name left out is hidden from the client (tab completion, highlighting), but the command still runs when typed. Names that are not in the list are ignored. member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.EntityChangeBlockEvent
member.summary: A mob (or a projectile, or a dying mob for its cobwebs) is about to change a block: an enderman takes or places a block, a sheep eats grass, a silverfish hides in stone, a ravager breaks leaves, a wither breaks blocks, a villager plants, a copper golem turns into a statue, a turtle or frog lays an egg, a mob tramples farmland, a mob breaks a door, a falling block starts to fall (entity none: the falling entity does not exist yet) or lands, an arrow douses fire, candles and campfires. Cancel = the block does not change (a falling block cancelled at its start stays where it is; cancelled at its landing it breaks without its item). Doors opened or closed by mobs are not reported (vanilla fires no change event for them); nor are explosions (EntityExplode), the ender dragon walls (EntityExplode) and snow golem trails (BlockForm).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.EntityTargetEvent
member.summary: A mob's target changed (set, switched or lost). Fired from the tick thread after the mob phases, once per change: the AI runs on worker threads, so a cancel cannot veto the change; it reverts it to the old target. A reverted goal may choose the same target again on the next tick and fire again. A rewritten target is applied only when it is a living entity of the mob's world that the mob may attack (a creative or spectator player is not), or 0 to clear the target; any other value keeps the old target. Applying it runs the mob kind's target rules, so the target can still be refused by the kind.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerSpawnLocationEvent
member.summary: The spawn of a joining player is chosen, before the spawn chunks are loaded. Fired on the tick thread (Paper's AsyncPlayerSpawnLocationEvent runs on the login thread; the server here does not allow a blocking handler on a network thread). A new player appears at a changed position in a changed world without the spawn search; a returning player appears at a changed position in a changed world, which replaces the saved one. Yaw and pitch are applied to a returning player and to a new player's join. Not cancellable. A non-finite position or rotation a handler wrote is ignored (the original is kept). The position is kept within |x| and |z| up to 29999984 and within the build height of the dimension it lands in; the pitch is kept within [-90, 90]; the yaw is wrapped to [-180, 180).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.ProfileWhitelistVerifyEvent
member.summary: The whitelist check of a login (PlayerList.canPlayerLogin), after the ban checks. Fired on every login that gets this far, whether or not the whitelist is on. Set Whitelisted to admit the profile or refuse it; a refused profile is disconnected with KickMessage. Fired on the tick thread. Not cancellable: change Whitelisted instead. Limitation: with enforce-whitelist on, a profile admitted here while it is not listed is disconnected by the next whitelist check (/whitelist remove, /whitelist on, /whitelist reload, /deop, or enforce-whitelist turned on), because those checks read the whitelist file alone. List the profile (WhitelistStateUpdate, whitelist_add) to keep it.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.ClockTimeSkipEvent
member.summary: A world clock is about to jump: the night skip of sleeping (only when it moves the overworld clock to the wake-up marker), /time set or /time add, or a plugin's world clock. Fired on the tick thread before the clock moves; a /time set to the time the clock already has does not fire it. Cancel to keep the clock where it is and send no clock update. A changed skip_amount is applied as an add to the current time. TimeSkip follows it for the same change (not after a cancel). Paper ClockTimeSkipEvent.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerTrackEntityEvent
member.summary: An entity is about to become visible to a player: it came into the player's tracking range, was just spawned near the player, or was shown again after Player.HideEntity, and its spawn packets are about to be sent to that client (Paper PlayerTrackEntityEvent). Fired on the tick thread once per pair, only while a handler listens, for players and for mobs, projectiles and items. Cancel to send nothing for this pair: the client does not see the entity, and the engine asks again in every following tick for as long as the entity stays in range. A hidden entity (Player.HideEntity) is never asked. The handler must not be slow: it runs for every pair that begins.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Http
member.summary: HTTP(S) for plugins. In the plugin worker the requests are performed by the server: its HTTP client resolves each name, refuses loopback, private, link-local and metadata addresses, limits request and response sizes and the rate, and enforces the timeouts (see the server's scripting.http.* settings in ramjet.toml). In an in-process host (development only) requests go out directly. Use , or new HttpClient(Http.Handler) for your own timeouts and headers. Do not dispose either: they are shared by every plugin.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Http.Handler
member.summary: The message handler behind every request. Share it; do not dispose it.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Http.Client
member.summary: A shared client over . Set the time limit per request with a ; the server applies its own total timeout as well. Do not dispose it.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.ItemStack
member.summary: An immutable item stack value: an item type, a count and data components. Every With... method returns a new stack; the value can be kept, compared and put into inventories, menus and the world (, , ).

remarks.para: Components are addressed by their registry key ("minecraft:custom_name") and carry NBT values. The ones the server converts are given in a plugin friendly form: text components (custom_name, item_name, lore lines) as JSON strings (what makes), integers (damage, max_damage, max_stack_size, repair_cost, map_id, enchantable, dyed_color), rarity as "common" .. "epic", enchantment_glint_override as a byte, unbreakable / glider as an empty compound, custom_data as a compound, item_model and tooltip_style as identifier strings, custom_model_data as {floats, flags, strings, colors}, enchantments and stored_enchantments as {"minecraft:sharpness": 3}, tooltip_display as {hide_tooltip, hidden_components}, use_cooldown as {seconds, group?} and food as {nutrition, saturation, can_always_eat}. Every other component the server knows is read as an opaque byte array holding its network encoding: it survives copying a stack but cannot be edited. A component key starting with ! removes a component of the item's prototype ().
A stack that no inventory accepts (unknown item, a count above the stack size, a component whose value does not convert) is refused by the call that receives it with an .

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.MenuClick
member.summary: A click in a . A menu is locked: a click that could move items out of the menu or into it (a slot of the menu, shift click, double click, number key, the off hand key, the drop key, a middle click) is denied and the client is resynced unless the handler calls ; always denies. Clicks that only touch the player's own inventory slots pass unless a handler cancels them (or the menu locks the player inventory too). The object is valid during the handler only.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.Menu
member.summary: A custom GUI: a container with icons and click handlers that the client shows like a chest, a hopper or a dispenser. The menu is owned by the plugin and closed for every viewer when the plugin unloads or reloads.

remarks.para: A menu is locked. The engine keeps it a display: a click that could take an icon out or put an item in is denied (and the whole menu resynced to the client) unless a handler allows it with ; drags over its slots, shift clicks, double clicks, number keys, the off hand key and the drop key cannot move items out of it or into it; the creative clone click gives no copy of an icon. Whatever a handler decides, the server is authoritative: it only performs what vanilla would perform for the click, and a cancelled click changes nothing.

Create menus with (plugin.Menus) or the static factories, which belong to the plugin whose code is running (OnEnable, an event handler, a command, a scheduled task); items in the slots are ordinary stacks, so the menu doubles as a small shared inventory (, ).

member.summary: Whether the entity makes no sound of its own (vanilla Silent): no ambient, hurt or death sounds. Any living entity.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.LivingEntity.Invulnerable
member.summary: Whether the entity takes no damage (vanilla Invulnerable). Any living entity. Hits whose damage type is tagged as bypassing invulnerability (such as falling into the void) and hits from a creative-mode player still land, as vanilla. It is separate from a player's creative invulnerability (the abilities), which also refuses damage on its own. A mob keeps the flag in its saved data (the NBT Invulnerable tag); a player's flag is runtime state only: it is not written to the player's save and does not survive a dimension change or a respawn.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.LivingEntity.Glowing
member.summary: Whether the entity glows (the outline in the team colour, white without a team) for every player online. The glow follows players who join or leave. The server keeps at most 64 plugin glows and the visuals table is shared: when there is no room, setting it does nothing, and the getter reads false until the glow reaches every viewer. Any living entity that the clients track.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Player.HideEntity(Mc.Scripting.Entity)
member.summary: Hides an entity from this player, for the plugin that is running (Paper Player.hideEntity). The player's client forgets the entity at once and the server does not send it to him again, however close it is, until it is shown. Hiding a player also removes him from this player's tab list (showing him adds the entry back before the entity is sent again). Hides are counted per plugin: the entity is visible again only when every plugin that hid it has called (or has unloaded). A plugin's hides end when it unloads. They are not saved: they end when either player leaves or the entity is removed.
member.remarks: fires when the entity was visible before (not when a second plugin hides it too); fires when the player was tracking it. Does nothing for a stale or untracked entity, for the player himself, for a player who is not online, and once the player already has 4096 hidden entities. A hidden entity is not asked . Needs a running plugin; use from code that runs outside one.
member.exception: No plugin is running.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Player.ShowEntity(Mc.Scripting.Entity)
member.summary: Takes back the running plugin's hide of an entity (Paper Player.showEntity). The entity is visible again only when no other plugin still hides it; then it is sent to the player when he is in range (the next tick; is asked then), a player's tab entry is added back first, and fires. Does nothing when this plugin had not hidden the entity.
member.exception: No plugin is running.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Loot.LootContext
member.summary: What a loot table is rolled with: the world, and the parameters the table's conditions and functions read (the vanilla LootParams).

remarks.para: Only the parameters the plugin API can name are here. Set the ones the table and its need; a table that needs one that is not set makes throw an naming it. Entities are handles: one that has died when the roll starts is an error too.

Killer also counts as the direct attacker (the melee case, as /loot kill rolls it). The damage type of a mob roll is what the kill was ("minecraft:player_attack", "minecraft:mob_attack", "minecraft:magic").

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Loot.LootTables.FillContainer(Mc.Scripting.Worlds.World,Mc.Scripting.BlockPos,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int64})
member.summary: Sets the loot table of a container (a chest, trapped chest, barrel or shulker box), the LootTable tag vanilla keeps in a container's NBT: the contents are rolled when the container is first opened, replacing what it held.
member.param: The block position of the container.
The seed of the roll (LootTableSeed); null means no seed: the table's random sequence rolls the contents when the container is opened.
member.returns: True when the container took the table; false when there is no block entity at the position, or it is not a chest, trapped chest, barrel or shulker box. Vanilla also lets hoppers, droppers, dispensers and crafters take a table, but the server does not roll those yet, so they return false.
member.exception: The table does not exist.

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.Nbt.NbtIo.DefaultQuota
member.summary: How much memory (in the accounting of the game's NbtAccounter: about 48 bytes per tag, plus strings and arrays) a read may build: 32 MiB. A few bytes of input can describe a very large tree (a list of a million empty compounds is one megabyte of data and a hundred megabytes of objects); the quota stops it.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Packets
member.summary: Typed packets: send a packet to a player, and observe, change or cancel the packets players send and the ones sent to them. The engine encodes every packet with its own codecs, so nothing malformed reaches a client.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Packets.On``1(System.Action{Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent{``0}},Mc.Scripting.PacketMode,Mc.Scripting.EventPriority)
member.summary: Subscribes to one packet type. In the handler sees a copy of each packet; in it may cancel the packet or change its fields. Handlers run in priority order (lowest first). A packet sent with is not seen: a plugin's own sends skip every plugin's handlers. Returns the subscription: dispose it to unsubscribe (also done when the plugin unloads).
member.exception: The packet cannot be observed or intercepted (its catalogue row has no such hook).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Packets.Send(Mc.Scripting.Player,Mc.Scripting.PacketBase)
member.summary: Sends a packet to a player. The packet is encoded by the engine, after the engine checks its values (ranges, registry ids, entity ids: an entity a plugin creates needs ). It is written in order with the engine's own packets of the tick. The packet does not reach the handlers of , this plugin's or another's.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider
member.summary: A file-based backend: groups (weighted, inheriting, with prefix and suffix) and per-player overrides, stored in a JSON file. The built-in backend () is permissions.json in the server directory; a provider created with another path reads and writes only that file. Resolution order: the player's own entries, then his groups by weight (highest first, parents after their child), then the implicit "default" group everybody belongs to. Within one layer the most specific node wins: an exact entry beats a.b.*, a longer wildcard beats a shorter one, * comes last; a false value is a denial. A key written as "-node" in the file means the same as "node": false.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Opens (and creates, when missing) a permission file at . A file that cannot be read (malformed JSON) does not stop the server: the provider starts empty (the registered defaults apply), logs the problem once and leaves the file alone so that it can be fixed and reloaded with . The file is written by this provider itself, so it works for any path the plugin can write; the server's own permissions.json is .

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.LoadError
member.summary: Why the file could not be read (null when it was, or since it was fixed and reloaded).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.Reload
member.summary: Re-reads the file (a missing file is created with a "default" and an "admin" group).
member.exception: The file is not valid JSON; the permissions in memory stay as they were.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.Save
member.summary: Writes the file if something changed, atomically (temp file, flushed, then renamed over the old one). The built-in backend's file is written by the engine (a host call: the worker's sandbox refuses writes to the server folder), and the engine refuses a write that comes too soon after the last one (its rate limit): then the changes stay pending and the next call (the runtime's flush, a second later) tries again. A provider on another path writes that file itself and never touches permissions.json. Never throws; a refusal or a failed write is logged once per streak and retried.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.NativePermissionTable
member.summary: Feeds the engine's permission table: declares node defaults, sets and changes the rules of a player, claims the table, and reads its statistics. The engine validates every message as a whole; a refused message changes nothing (the status is the host call's: 0 applied, -1 malformed, -2 oversize, -3 refused, -4 version gap, -5 unknown kind). While a claim is held the engine answers the permission requirements of commands from the table; the rules describe a player's permissions, and a player whose rules were never sent gets the defaults.

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.NativePermissionTable.Any

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.PermissionManager
member.summary: The server's permission system: declared nodes with defaults, the active backend () and the question "does this player have this node?". The default backend is a on permissions.json; a plugin may replace it.
member.remarks: Resolution: the provider's explicit value (wildcards, groups and player overrides are its business); if it has no opinion, the node's registered default decides ( and friends are evaluated against the player's vanilla operator level); an unregistered node without an entry is denied, except minecraft.command.<name> which defaults to the vanilla operator level of that command. The console always has every permission. Everything here runs on the tick thread.

member.returns: A task for the work (exceptions are also logged with the plugin's name).

member.summary: Runs on the .NET thread pool.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Scheduler.ToTick
member.summary: Awaitable that always resumes on the tick thread at the next tick boundary, even when already there: await Scheduler.ToTick(); (a wait loop such as while (!loaded) await Scheduler.ToTick(); needs this). Use to skip the hop when already on the tick thread. If the plugin unloads first the continuation is dropped.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Scheduler.EnsureTick
member.summary: Awaitable that resumes on the tick thread: await Scheduler.EnsureTick();. Already on the tick thread it continues synchronously (no hop); otherwise it resumes at the next tick boundary, like . If the plugin unloads first the continuation is dropped.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Scheduler.ToAsync
member.summary: Awaitable that always resumes on a thread-pool thread: await Scheduler.ToAsync(); (leave the tick thread before blocking work).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Scheduler.Delay(System.Int64)
member.summary: Completes on the tick thread after ticks: await Scheduler.Delay(1);. Awaited right away (the normal case: the task is not complete at the await), the continuation runs inline on the tick thread when the delay completes it. member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Server.DispatchCommand(System.String)
member.summary: Runs a command line as the console: operator level 4, with the feedback in the server log. The line is the command as a player types it, with or without the leading slash, and it goes through the server's command dispatcher, so vanilla and plugin commands both run.
member.remarks:
Nothing is sent to the chat and no chat event fires: does not fire either (as Paper's dispatchCommand does not fire PlayerCommandPreprocessEvent). No API fires it for a line a plugin runs: a plugin that wants its effect does that work itself. A line that is too long, has a control character, or names an unknown command fails with a message and runs nothing. A dispatch may run another command (an execute that runs one), up to 8 levels deep; deeper fails.
When the plugins run in the plugin worker process, a dispatch made by a plugin cannot run a plugin command: the worker is blocked in this call and cannot run its own command meanwhile, so that command fails with a message. Vanilla commands still run, and so does a plugin command the server runs by itself (a player's typed command, a command block). To run a plugin's own command, call its code directly.
Inside an event handler, a system, a scheduler phase or another plugin's call this fails with a message and runs nothing: use there.
member.param: The command line (at most 32767 characters after an optional leading slash).
member.returns: The outcome: success, the command's result, and the failure message when it failed.
member.exception: Called off the tick thread.
is null.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Server.DispatchCommand(Mc.Scripting.Player,System.String)
member.summary: Runs a command line as a player: the player's own permissions decide what runs, and the feedback goes to the player's chat, as when the player types it. The line is limited to 256 characters (a chat line), with or without the leading slash. See for the rules (including that no fires); a player who is offline fails at once. Inside an event handler, a system, a scheduler phase or another plugin's call it fails with a message and runs nothing: use there.
member.param: The player who runs the command.
The command line (at most 256 characters after an optional leading slash).
member.returns: The outcome: success, the command's result, and the failure message when it failed.
member.exception: Called off the tick thread.
or is null.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Server.DispatchCommandAsync(System.String)
member.summary: Queues a command line to run as the console and returns a task for its outcome. Unlike it works for plugin commands too: the line runs at the end of the next tick, when the plugin worker is not in a call.
member.remarks: Like , no fires for the line. The task completes on the tick thread a tick after the line ran. At most 64 lines are accepted per tick and 1024 are pending; beyond that the task completes at once with a failure. A line queued by a command that runs from a queued line is one level deeper; a line nested more than 8 levels fails.
member.param: The command line (at most 32767 characters after an optional leading slash).
member.returns: A task that completes with the outcome.
member.exception: Called off the tick thread.
is null.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Services.IWhitelist
member.summary: The server's whitelist: the vanilla file whitelist.json, and the two switches that enforce it (white-list and enforce-whitelist in server.properties). A player who is not on the list (and is not an operator) cannot join while is on. With on, the online players who are not on the list are kicked, operators included, as the list or a switch makes them unlisted; this is vanilla's kickUnlistedPlayers, which looks at the list only. Offline players work: the uuid is the key, and resolves a name. Adding a player and the switches are written at once to the server's files; a script's additions and removals are written a few seconds later, with the ban lists (a plugin never saves them itself). Each change is logged with the plugin that made it. Thread: tick thread.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Services.IWhitelist.Enabled
member.summary: Whether the whitelist is in force (white-list in server.properties). Setting it writes server.properties, as /whitelist on and off do; turning it on kicks the unlisted players when is on.

member.summary: Whether unlisted online players are kicked (enforce-whitelist in server.properties), operators included. Turning it on kicks them at once when is on.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Services.IWhitelist.Contains(Mc.Scripting.Uuid)

member.returns: True when the uuid is listed.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Services.IWhitelist.Add(Mc.Scripting.Uuid,System.String)
member.summary: Adds a player to the list (kicks nobody). The write is deferred a few seconds, with the ban lists.
member.param: The player's name: 1 to 16 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and underscore.
member.returns: True when the player was added; false when the uuid was listed already, a new entry beyond access.max_whitelist_entries, or a name the engine refuses.
member.exception: The name is empty, longer than 16 characters, or has a character outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and underscore.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Services.IWhitelist.Remove(Mc.Scripting.Uuid)
member.summary: Removes a player from the list (the write is deferred like ), then kicks the online players who are no longer listed when and are on (as /whitelist remove does).

member.summary: Writes the pending additions and removals, then reads whitelist.json again (as /whitelist reload does), then kicks the unlisted online players when is on. A file that cannot be read leaves the list as it was.

member.summary: Registers a system in the engine's registry. The registry name is namespaced by the plugin: "{plugin name}:{name}" (left as is when already starts with that prefix), so plugins cannot collide; a collision with a native system or with another plugin's system throws. names an existing (native or scripted) system for After/Before/Replace (the phase is then the anchor's and is ignored). member.summary: The datapack tags of the blocks, items, entity types and biomes: #minecraft:logs and the like. The tag names are given with or without the leading #; the keys are "namespace:path" (the namespace may be left out for minecraft).

remarks.para: Membership answers what the datapack says, including the tags that name other tags. An unknown tag or key is simply not a member (no exception): a tag lists nothing. Tags are read on the tick thread (the loot service is single threaded).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Worlds.World.SpawnEntity(System.String,Mc.Scripting.Vec3d,Mc.Scripting.Nbt.NbtCompound,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Spawns an entity of a type, like /summon. Mobs the engine simulates (zombies, cows, creepers ...) get their normal spawn logic: with no NBT their random attributes and equipment are rolled; with NBT the data is applied as given ({Health:5f,CustomName:'"Bob"'}). Item entities (minecraft:item with Item:{id:"minecraft:diamond",count:3}) and experience orbs (minecraft:experience_orb with Value) are supported too. The spawn fires (reason Plugin) where the entity kind has that event, and a handler may cancel it.
member.param: The entity type key, "minecraft:zombie" (the namespace may be left out).
The initial yaw in degrees (an NBT Rotation overrides it).
member.returns: The entity (a handle: check before keeping it), or when the type is unknown or cannot be spawned here (a type the engine does not simulate yet, the chunk is not loaded, a monster in peaceful, a handler cancelled it).

member.summary: Every entity of the dimension (players, mobs, item entities, experience orbs, projectiles, falling blocks ...). A snapshot: entities that spawn or vanish afterwards are not reflected.

member.summary: The players in the dimension.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Worlds.World.Explode(Mc.Scripting.Vec3d,System.Single,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,Mc.Scripting.Entity)
member.summary: Creates an explosion like a creeper's: it damages and pushes entities (with exposure and distance falloff), destroys blocks (dropping loot, with decay), optionally lights fires, and the clients get the particles and the sound.
member.remarks: Events (as Paper's createExplosion): with true, fires when is an entity and when it is none. They fire after the entities are hurt; a cancel protects the blocks and the fire. The event's block list holds the positions the explosion's rays reach (air included, as in vanilla), so in practice it fires whenever is true, even when no block is destroyed. With it false nothing fires. is not fired.
member.param: The radius-like strength (TNT is 4, a creeper 3, a charged creeper 6; the work grows with its cube, so values above 32 are refused).
Whether fires start in the explosion's wake.
Whether blocks are destroyed (false: only the entities are affected).
The entity that causes it (excluded from the damage, used as the damage source), or none.
member.returns: True when the explosion happened; false for a power outside 0-32 (exclusive of 0), an unloaded centre or an unknown world.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Worlds.WorldBorder
member.summary: The world border of a dimension: the square the players are meant to stay in (vanilla's WorldBorder, the state /worldborder changes). Outside it a living entity takes damage per block beyond the safe zone, the collision of entities stops at it, and the clients draw it. Every setter goes through the same engine path as the command: the clients get the matching packets at once, the border is used by the physics from the next tick, and it is saved with the world. Get it from ; it is a light view of the dimension's border (nothing is cached), so reading it again is cheap. This is the server's border. The client-only packets Packets.Clientbound.SetBorderCenter, SetBorderSize and SetBorderLerpSize change only what one client draws; they do not move this border.
member.remarks: Everything here must be called on the tick thread ( otherwise). Values outside the command's limits throw before anything changes.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Worlds.WorldBorder.SetSize(System.Double,System.Int64)
member.summary: Sets the size of the border, like /worldborder set <size> <time>. With 0 the size changes at once (the clients are told the new size); above 0 the border moves to over that time, the size being interpolated every tick (the clients are told the target and the time). The time is rounded up to whole ticks (50 ms each). Setting the current size is a no-op, like the command's "nochange": nothing is sent, and a border that is moving keeps moving (the current size is the interpolated one, so the no-op also holds while a lerp runs).
member.param: The new size in blocks across: 1 to .
How long the border takes to get there, in milliseconds; 0 for at once.
member.exception: The size is not finite or outside 1 to , or the time is negative.
